# Interface: TypeSafeClientConfig
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/api/interfaces/TypeSafeClientConfig

Client options. Explicit values take precedence over environment variables, then SDK defaults.

## Properties

### apiKey?

```ts theme={null}
optional apiKey?: string;
```

Required API key; falls back to `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.

***

### baseURL?

```ts theme={null}
optional baseURL?: string;
```

API root; falls back to `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL`, then `https://api.typesafe.ai`.

***

### compression?

```ts theme={null}
optional compression?: Compression;
```

Request body compression, sent as `Content-Encoding`. Default: `"zstd"` on runtimes that
have it (Node.js 22.15 or newer), otherwise `false`. Bodies under 1 KiB are always sent
uncompressed. Pass `false` to send all bodies uncompressed, for example to an API that
doesn't accept compressed requests.

***

### dangerouslyAllowBrowser?

```ts theme={null}
optional dangerouslyAllowBrowser?: boolean;
```

Allow browser use, exposing the API key to page users. Default: false.

***

### defaultHeaders?

```ts theme={null}
optional defaultHeaders?: Record<string, string>;
```

Additional request headers; per-call headers take precedence.

***

### defaultModel?

```ts theme={null}
optional defaultModel?: string;
```

Default model; falls back to `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL`, then `jev-latest`.

***

### fetch?

```ts theme={null}
optional fetch?: Fetch;
```

Custom HTTP fetch implementation for transport configuration or tests. Default: global `fetch`.

***

### logger?

```ts theme={null}
optional logger?: Logger;
```

Logger filtered to `logLevel` and above. Default: prefixed `console`.

***

### logLevel?

```ts theme={null}
optional logLevel?: LogLevel;
```

Log level; falls back to `TYPESAFE_LOG_LEVEL`, then `warn`.
`info` logs request summaries; `debug` adds headers and bodies.
Known credential headers are redacted; bodies are not.

***

### retry?

```ts theme={null}
optional retry?: Partial<RetryPolicy>;
```

Retry overrides; omitted fields use the defaults in `RetryPolicy`.

***

### timeout?

```ts theme={null}
optional timeout?: number;
```

Timeout per attempt in milliseconds, without a total retry budget. Default: 10000.

# Variable: withAssets
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/api/variables/withAssets

```ts theme={null}
const withAssets: {
(strings, ...values): TextWithAssets;
  join: TextWithAssets;
};
```

Tag a template literal so the assets interpolated into it are sent with the text.

Each asset is replaced by its reference; other values are converted to strings, as in an
untagged template literal. To write a list of assets with a separator, use
`withAssets.join`.

## Type Declaration

## Parameters

### strings

`TemplateStringsArray`

### values

...readonly `unknown`\[]

## Returns

[`TextWithAssets`](/sdk/javascript/api/interfaces/TextWithAssets)

### join()

```ts theme={null}
join(values, separator?): TextWithAssets;
```

Join `values` with `separator`, as `Array.prototype.join` does, and send the assets among
them with the text. The result can be passed as content or interpolated into `withAssets`.

#### Parameters

##### values

readonly `unknown`\[]

##### separator?

`string`

Written between values. Default: `","`.

#### Returns

[`TextWithAssets`](/sdk/javascript/api/interfaces/TextWithAssets)

#### Example

```ts theme={null}
const { answers } = await client.systemOne({
  state: withAssets`The seller uploaded ${withAssets.join(uploads, ", ")}.`,
  questions: { same: noul("Do the uploads show the same product?") },
});
```

## Example

```ts theme={null}
const { answers } = await client.systemOne({
  state: withAssets`Compare ${photo} with the listing.`,
  questions: { same: noul(withAssets`Is ${photo} the product in ${listing}?`) },
});
```


# Changelog
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/changelog

## v0.7.0 (2026-10-14)

### Breaking changes

* require Node.js 22 or newer
* stop exporting request payload types

### Features

* support images, as an experimental feature enabled with the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true` header: create them with `image()` or `Image.fromBase64()`, then place them in `state`, question instructions, or criteria, write them into text with `withAssets` and `withAssets.join`, or reference them by names you choose in `assets`
* add `box` questions, which locate what their instructions describe in an image; use them with the `jev-preview` model
* compress request bodies of 1 KiB or more with zstd on Node.js 22.15 or newer; pass `compression: false` to send them uncompressed

### Bug fixes

* allow null token counts in usage
* add more request validation checks
* reject the returned promise for invalid requests instead of throwing
* accept score criteria lists built at runtime
* stop an unhandled rejection on Node.js 22 when a request times out or is aborted mid-body

## v0.6.0 (2026-09-15)

### Breaking changes

* accept `Score.criteria` as an ordered sequence instead of a dictionary keyed by integers

## v0.5.7 (2026-09-11)

This is the initial public release of TypeSafe JavaScript and TypeScript SDK. Learn more in the [documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/js-sdk).


# TypeSafe Python SDK
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python

Install the TypeSafe Python SDK and get started with asynchronous or synchronous API calls.

Browse the [Python SDK source on GitHub](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python).

Asynchronous and synchronous Python clients for the [TypeSafe](https://typesafe.ai) API. Learn how to use TypeSafe [here](https://docs.typesafe.ai/).

## Quickstart

1. Install the SDK:

   > [tab] uv
   >
   > ```sh theme={null}
   > uv add typesafe-sdk
   > ```

   > [tab] pip
   >
   > ```sh theme={null}
   > pip install typesafe-sdk
   > ```

   Extras (for example, `typesafe-sdk[http2]`) supported:

   * `http2`: enable [HTTP/2 support](/sdk/python/usage/advanced#http2)
   * `pil`: send [Pillow images](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Image.from_pil)
   * `zstd`: [compress request bodies](/sdk/python/usage/advanced#ensure-zstd-is-available) on Python 3.13 and earlier
2. Set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in your environment (create it [here](https://console.typesafe.ai/))
3. Call the System One API:

   > [tab] Async
   >
   > With [AsyncTypeSafeClient](/sdk/python/api/clients/async):
   >
   > ```python theme={null}
   > from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Choice, Noul, Score
   >
   >
   > async def main() -> None:
   >     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
   >         response = await client.system_one(
   >             state={"document": "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP."},
   >             questions={
   >                 "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this ticket about billing?"),
   >                 "tone": Choice(
   >                     instructions="What is the customer's tone?",
   >                     criteria={"calm": None, "frustrated": None, "angry": None},
   >                 ),
   >                 "urgency": Score(
   >                     instructions="How urgent is this ticket?",
   >                     criteria=["can wait", "this week", "today"],
   >                 ),
   >             },
   >         )
   >
   >     print(response.nouls["billing"].noul)
   >     print(response.choices["tone"].choice)
   >     print(response.scores["urgency"].score)
   > ```

   > [tab] Sync
   >
   > With [TypeSafeClient](/sdk/python/api/clients/sync):
   >
   > ```python theme={null}
   > from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, Score, TypeSafeClient
   >
   > with TypeSafeClient() as client:
   >     response = client.system_one(
   >         state={"document": "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP."},
   >         questions={
   >             "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this ticket about billing?"),
   >             "tone": Choice(
   >                 instructions="What is the customer's tone?",
   >                 criteria={"calm": None, "frustrated": None, "angry": None},
   >             ),
   >             "urgency": Score(
   >                 instructions="How urgent is this ticket?",
   >                 criteria=["can wait", "this week", "today"],
   >             ),
   >         },
   >     )
   >
   > print(response.nouls["billing"].noul)
   > print(response.choices["tone"].choice)
   > print(response.scores["urgency"].score)
   > ```

# Asynchronous client
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/clients/async

Use AsyncTypeSafeClient to ask questions, list models, and configure asynchronous TypeSafe API requests.

## typesafe\_sdk.AsyncTypeSafeClient

Copy signature
<pre aria-label="SDK signature">`AsyncTypeSafeClient(
&#x20;   \*,
&#x20;   api\_key: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   model: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   retry: [RetryPolicy](/sdk/python/api/retries#typesafe_sdk.RetryPolicy) | None = None,
&#x20;   timeout: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)
&#x20;   | httpx2.Timeout
&#x20;   | None = None,
&#x20;   headers: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)\[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | None = None,
&#x20;   transport: httpx2.AsyncBaseTransport
&#x20;   | None = None,
&#x20;   http\_client: httpx2.[AsyncClient](https://pydantic.dev/docs/httpx2/api/api/#httpx2.AsyncClient)
&#x20;   | None = None,
&#x20;   base\_url: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   compression: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)\["zstd", False]
&#x20;   | None = None,
)`</pre>

Create an asynchronous HTTP client for [TypeSafe AI API](https://typesafe.ai).

Explicit options take precedence over environment variables; empty or whitespace-only environment values are ignored.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Logging setup**
>
> The SDK logs to the `typesafe_sdk` logger; configure it through standard logging, or set `TYPESAFE_LOG_LEVEL` (`debug`, `info`, ...) for a quick default. Secret headers are redacted from log output; request and response bodies are not.

Parameters:

* **`api_key`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Required API key; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` environment variable. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped. Empty keys, internal whitespace, control characters, and non-ASCII characters are rejected.
* **`model`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Model name; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` environment variable.
* **`retry`** (`RetryPolicy | None`, default: `None` ) –

  A `RetryPolicy` controlling retry behavior; see `RetryPolicy` for the available options and their defaults. Pass `RetryPolicy(max_retries=0)` to disable retries.
* **`timeout`** (`float | httpx2.Timeout | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Timeout for HTTP operations. Inherits `http_client.timeout` when supplied, otherwise the SDK default.
* **`headers`** (`Mapping[str, str] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Additional request headers to set.
* **`transport`** (`httpx2.AsyncBaseTransport | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Optional custom HTTP transport, closed when this SDK client closes.
* **`http_client`** (`httpx2.AsyncClient | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Optional `httpx2.AsyncClient`; mutually exclusive with `transport`. Closed when this SDK client closes.
* **`base_url`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  API root; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` environment variable.
* **`compression`** (`Literal['zstd', False] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Request body compression: `"zstd"`, or `False` to send bodies uncompressed. Defaults to zstd [when available](/sdk/python/usage/advanced#ensure-zstd-is-available).

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  The API key is missing or invalid, the timeout is invalid, or zstd compression is unavailable.
* `ValueError` –

  Both `transport` and `http_client` are supplied.

Examples:

```python theme={null}
import asyncio

from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Choice, Noul


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
        result = await client.system_one(
            state="I was charged twice. Please help.",
            questions={
                "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?"),
                "tone": Choice(
                    instructions="What is the tone?",
                    criteria={"calm": None, "angry": None},
                ),
            },
        )
        assert 0 <= result.nouls["billing"].noul <= 1
        assert result.choices["tone"].choice in {"calm", "angry"}


asyncio.run(main())
```

### attach\_assets

Copy signature
<pre aria-label="SDK signature">`attach\_assets(
&#x20;   assets: [Asset](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Asset) | [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)\[[Asset](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Asset)],
) -> [AbstractContextManager](https://docs.python.org/3/library/contextlib.html#contextlib.AbstractContextManager)\[None]`</pre>

Attach assets to calls made within a `with` block, for referencing them inside strings.

Until the block exits, calls on this client send each attached asset whose reference, `str(asset)`, appears in the request.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Warning**
>
> The SDK only recognizes references to assets that are attached, passed in `assets`, or placed directly in the content. A reference to any other asset is sent as plain text, without the asset.

Parameters:

* **`assets`** (`Asset | Sequence[Asset]`) –

  An asset, or a sequence of them.

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  An attached value is not an asset.

Examples:

```python theme={null}
from pathlib import Path

from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse


async def inspect(client: AsyncTypeSafeClient, path: Path) -> SystemOneResponse:
    photo = Image(path)
    with client.attach_assets(photo):
        return await client.system_one(
            state=f"Product: {photo}",
            questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the product damaged?")},
        )
```

> &#x20;   extra\_body: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)\[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [JSONValue](/sdk/python/api/types/common#typesafe_sdk.JSONValue) | None]
> &#x20;   | None = None,
> &#x20;   response\_model: [type](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)\[ResponseT],
> ) -> ResponseT`</pre>

Answer named questions about text, structured state, or assets.

See [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/system-one) for details.

Parameters:

* **`state`** (`Content`) –

  Text, an asset, a JSON object, or an array to evaluate. See [state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/state) for details.
* **`questions`** (`Mapping[str, Question]`) –

  Nonempty mapping of names to question objects or raw dictionaries.
* **`model`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Model override; `None` inherits the client default.
* **`assets`** (`Mapping[str, Asset] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Assets keyed by the reference used for them in `state` or questions; see [Attaching media assets](/sdk/python/usage/basic#attaching-media-assets).
* **`retry`** (`RetryPolicy | None`, default: `None` ) –

  An optional retry policy to override the client-level value for this call only.
* **`timeout`** (`float | httpx2.Timeout | None`, default: `None` ) –

  An optional timeout for http operations to override the client-level value for this call only, in seconds.
* **`extra_headers`** (`Mapping[str, str] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Additional request headers to set.
* **`extra_body`** (`Mapping[str, JSONValue | None] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Additional top-level request-body fields, shallow-merged over the body after `state`, `model`, `questions`, and `assets` are set. Merging is last-write-wins: a key that collides with those fields overrides it, and object values are replaced rather than deep-merged.
* **`response_model`** (`type[ResponseT] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Optional Pydantic `BaseModel` type describing the JSON response body, including any nested answer models.

Returns:

* `SystemOneResponse | ResponseT` –

  An instance of `response_model`, or `SystemOneResponse` with answers keyed by question
* `SystemOneResponse | ResponseT` –

  name and model and token usage details when no custom model is supplied.

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  The request is invalid before it's sent, such as empty questions or an unreadable asset.
* `TypeSafeAPIError` –

  The server returns an unsuccessful HTTP response after any retries.
* `TypeSafeAPIConnectionError` –

  The request cannot connect or times out after any retries.
* `TypeSafeAPIResponseValidationError` –

  The response body does not match the response model.

Examples:

Create questions with named arguments:

```python theme={null}
async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
        result = await client.system_one(
            state="I was charged twice. Please help.",
            questions={
                "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?"),
                "tone": Choice(
                    instructions="What is the tone?",
                    criteria={"calm": None, "angry": None},
                ),
            },
        )
        assert 0 <= result.nouls["billing"].noul <= 1
        assert result.choices["tone"].choice in {"calm", "angry"}
```

Pass questions as dictionaries:

```python theme={null}
async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
        result = await client.system_one(
            state={"message": "I was charged twice. Please help."},
            questions={
                "billing": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this about billing?"},
                "tone": {
                    "type": "choice",
                    "instructions": "What is the tone?",
                    "criteria": {"calm": None, "angry": None},
                },
            },
        )
        assert 0 <= result.nouls["billing"].noul <= 1
        assert result.choices["tone"].choice in {"calm", "angry"}
```

## typesafe\_sdk.TypeSafeClient

Copy signature
<pre aria-label="SDK signature">`TypeSafeClient(
&#x20;   \*,
&#x20;   api\_key: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   model: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   retry: [RetryPolicy](/sdk/python/api/retries#typesafe_sdk.RetryPolicy) | None = None,
&#x20;   timeout: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)
&#x20;   | httpx2.Timeout
&#x20;   | None = None,
&#x20;   headers: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)\[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | None = None,
&#x20;   transport: httpx2.BaseTransport
&#x20;   | None = None,
&#x20;   http\_client: httpx2.[Client](https://pydantic.dev/docs/httpx2/api/api/#httpx2.Client) | None = None,
&#x20;   base\_url: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | None = None,
&#x20;   compression: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)\["zstd", False]
&#x20;   | None = None,
)`</pre>

Create an HTTP client for [TypeSafe AI API](https://typesafe.ai).

Explicit options take precedence over environment variables; empty or whitespace-only environment values are ignored.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Logging setup**
>
> The SDK logs to the `typesafe_sdk` logger; configure it through standard logging, or set `TYPESAFE_LOG_LEVEL` (`debug`, `info`, ...) for a quick default. Secret headers are redacted from log output; request and response bodies are not.

Parameters:

* **`api_key`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Required API key; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` environment variable. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped. Empty keys, internal whitespace, control characters, and non-ASCII characters are rejected.
* **`model`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Model name; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` environment variable.
* **`retry`** (`RetryPolicy | None`, default: `None` ) –

  A `RetryPolicy` controlling retry behavior; see `RetryPolicy` for the available options and their defaults. Pass `RetryPolicy(max_retries=0)` to disable retries.
* **`timeout`** (`float | httpx2.Timeout | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Timeout for HTTP operations. Inherits `http_client.timeout` when supplied, otherwise the SDK default.
* **`headers`** (`Mapping[str, str] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Additional request headers to set.
* **`transport`** (`httpx2.BaseTransport | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Optional custom HTTP transport, closed when this SDK client closes.
* **`http_client`** (`httpx2.Client | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Optional `httpx2.Client`; mutually exclusive with `transport`. Closed when this SDK client closes.
* **`base_url`** (`str | None`, default: `None` ) –

  API root; may be set via the `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` environment variable.
* **`compression`** (`Literal['zstd', False] | None`, default: `None` ) –

  Request body compression: `"zstd"`, or `False` to send bodies uncompressed. Defaults to zstd [when available](/sdk/python/usage/advanced#ensure-zstd-is-available).

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  The API key is missing or invalid, the timeout is invalid, or zstd compression is unavailable.
* `ValueError` –

  Both `transport` and `http_client` are supplied.

Examples:

```python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    result = client.system_one(
        state="I was charged twice. Please help.",
        questions={
            "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?"),
            "tone": Choice(
                instructions="What is the tone?",
                criteria={"calm": None, "angry": None},
            ),
        },
    )
    assert 0 <= result.nouls["billing"].noul <= 1
    assert result.choices["tone"].choice in {"calm", "angry"}
```

### attach\_assets

Copy signature
<pre aria-label="SDK signature">`attach\_assets(
&#x20;   assets: [Asset](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Asset) | [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)\[[Asset](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Asset)],
) -> [AbstractContextManager](https://docs.python.org/3/library/contextlib.html#contextlib.AbstractContextManager)\[None]`</pre>

Attach assets to calls made within a `with` block, for referencing them inside strings.

Until the block exits, calls on this client send each attached asset whose reference, `str(asset)`, appears in the request.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Warning**
>
> The SDK only recognizes references to assets that are attached, passed in `assets`, or placed directly in the content. A reference to any other asset is sent as plain text, without the asset.

Parameters:

* **`assets`** (`Asset | Sequence[Asset]`) –

  An asset, or a sequence of them.

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  An attached value is not an asset.

Examples:

```python theme={null}
from pathlib import Path

from typesafe_sdk import Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse, TypeSafeClient


def inspect(client: TypeSafeClient, path: Path) -> SystemOneResponse:
    photo = Image(path)
    with client.attach_assets(photo):
        return client.system_one(
            state=f"Product: {photo}",
            questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the product damaged?")},
        )
```

### status

# Assets
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/types/assets

Attach assets to System One requests and reference them from request content.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note**
>
> The API detects each image's format from its bytes.

## typesafe\_sdk.Asset

`module-attribute`

Copy signature

<pre aria-label="SDK signature">
  \`Asset

  :

  &#x20;

  [TypeAlias](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypeAlias)

  &#x20;

  \=

  &#x20;

  [Image](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Image)\`
</pre>

An asset referenced from request content; currently only images are supported.

## typesafe\_sdk.Image

`dataclass`

Copy signature

<pre aria-label="SDK signature">
  \`Image

  (

  data

  :

  &#x20;

  [Buffer](https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html#typing_extensions.Buffer)

  &#x20;

  |

  &#x20;

  [PathLike](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)

  \[

  [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

  ])\`
</pre>

An image asset backed by image file bytes, or a path to an image file.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Reusing images**
>
> An `Image` is loaded once, on first use, and reused by every request that sends the same `Image` object.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Working with `Buffer` objects**
>
> `Image` also accepts `Buffer` objects: anything exposing its memory through the [buffer protocol](https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/buffer.html), such as `bytearray`, `memoryview`, `mmap`, or NumPy arrays. Buffers other than `bytes` are copied into memory once, on first use, so the original can change or be closed afterwards.

Examples:

From a file path:

```python theme={null}
from pathlib import Path

image = Image(Path("photos/product.png"))
```

From bytes in memory:

```python theme={null}
def from_bytes(data: bytes) -> Image:
    return Image(data)
```

From base64 text, such as an upload:

```python theme={null}
def from_upload(data_base64: str) -> Image:
    return Image.from_base64(data_base64)
```

From a Pillow image (requires the `pil` extra):

```python theme={null}
import PIL.Image

image = Image.from_pil(PIL.Image.new("RGB", (64, 64)), format="jpeg")
```

From a slice of a larger buffer, without copying it into `bytes` first:

```python theme={null}
def embedded_photo(container: bytes, offset: int, length: int) -> Image:
    return Image(memoryview(container)[offset : offset + length])
```

From a memory-mapped file:

```python theme={null}
import mmap


def map_photo(path: Path) -> Image:
    with path.open("rb") as file:
        return Image(mmap.mmap(file.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ))
```

### data

`instance-attribute`

Copy signature

<pre aria-label="SDK signature">
  \`data

  :

  &#x20;

  [Buffer](https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html#typing_extensions.Buffer)

  &#x20;

  |

  &#x20;

  [PathLike](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)

  \[

  [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

  ]\`
</pre>

Image contents, represented as one of:

* raw bytes (anything supporting the [`Buffer` protocol](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#buffer-objects))
* [path-like](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) object pointing at the image on the filesystem

### from\_base64

`classmethod`

Copy signature

<pre aria-label="SDK signature">
  \`from\_base64

  (

  data

  :

  &#x20;

  [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

  &#x20;

  |

  &#x20;

  [Buffer](https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html#typing_extensions.Buffer)

  )

  &#x20;

  ->

  &#x20;

  [Self](https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html#typing_extensions.Self)\`
</pre>

Create an `Image` instance from a base64-encoded image bytes.

Parameters:

* **`data`** (`str | Buffer`) –

  The image file bytes, base64-encoded, as text or an ASCII buffer. Whitespace, such as the line breaks of wrapped base64, is ignored.

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  The data isn't valid base64 text.

### from\_pil

`classmethod`

Copy signature
<pre aria-label="SDK signature">`from\_pil(
&#x20;   image: [PIL](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/PIL.html#module-PIL).[Image](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html#module-PIL.Image).[Image](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html#PIL.Image.Image), format: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) = "jpeg"
) -> [Self](https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html#typing_extensions.Self)`</pre>

Create an `Image` instance from a [Pillow](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/) image.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Encoder settings**
>
> The image is saved with Pillow's default encoder settings, except that JPEG uses quality 95. JPEG can't store transparency or palettes, so pass `format="png"` for RGBA or P mode images. Encode it yourself if different settings are needed.

Parameters:

* **`image`** (`PIL.Image.Image`) –

  The Pillow image to encode.
* **`format`** (`str`, default: `'jpeg'` ) –

  The image format to save as, by its [Pillow name](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/handbook/image-file-formats.html).

Raises:

* `TypeSafeError` –

  Pillow can't encode the image in this format.

# Questions

Provide state and ask yes/no, choice, and score questions using objects or dictionaries.

## State

`state` is the text or JSON object you want to ask questions about. It cannot be `None`, but values inside an object may be `None`.

## Question objects

Use `Noul`, `Choice`, `Score`, and `Box` to define questions with named arguments.

## typesafe\_sdk.Box

`pydantic-model`

Bases: `_Question`, `wire.BoxQuestion`

A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's image.

Examples:

```python theme={null}
from pathlib import Path

from typesafe_sdk import Box, BoxAnswer, Image, TypeSafeClient


def locate_dog(client: TypeSafeClient, photo: Path) -> BoxAnswer:
    result = client.system_one(
        state=Image(photo),
        questions={"dog": Box(instructions="The dog")},
        model="jev-preview",
    )
    return result.boxes["dog"]
```

## Question dictionaries

Question dictionaries include a `type` key: `"noul"`, `"choice"`, `"score"`, or `"box"`. You can mix dictionaries and question objects in the same request.

### Bug fixes

* prevent async client crashes during concurrent TLS connections with `truststore<=0.10.4`
* add more request validation checks

### Documentation

* add a new Performance section with tips for high-concurrency usage

### Performance

* update the default settings to keep all pooled connections alive for 30 seconds

## v0.7.2 (2026-09-26)

### Miscellaneous

* add `http2` extra to `typesafe-sdk` package

### Documentation

* document `typesafe-sdk` usage with HTTP/2 support

### Documentation

# Advanced usage
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/usage/advanced

Performance tuning, logging, and forward compatibility for the TypeSafe Python SDK.

## Performance

If your application sends hundreds of requests per second, follow these recommendations.

### Reuse clients

Make sure to reuse a client instance when sending multiple requests. Setting up a new client involves the overhead of starting new connections and TLS handshakes.

### Ensure `zstd` is available

The clients compress request bodies of 1 KiB or more with [zstd](https://facebook.github.io/zstd/), which reduces upload size and time, especially for large states.

Make sure `zstd` is installed on Python versions earlier than 3.14:

```shell theme={null}
uv add "typesafe-sdk[zstd]"
```

Compression can be configured or disabled via the `compression` client constructor argument.

### Use `aiohttp` for async code

For async code at high request rates, pass an [aiohttp](https://docs.aiohttp.org/)-based HTTP client from [`httpx-aiohttp`](https://pypi.org/project/httpx-aiohttp/):

```shell theme={null}
uv add "httpx-aiohttp[httpx2]"
```

```python theme={null}
from httpx_aiohttp.httpx2 import Httpx2AiohttpClient

from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient

client = AsyncTypeSafeClient(http_client=Httpx2AiohttpClient())
```

### Create a client per thread

`TypeSafeClient` can be shared between threads, but under heavy load its connection pool becomes the bottleneck. Create one client per thread and reuse it for every request that thread sends.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Example**
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import threading
>
> from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient
>
>
> class ThreadClients(threading.local):
>     def __init__(self) -> None:
>         self.client = TypeSafeClient()
>
>
> clients = ThreadClients()
>
> # In any thread, `clients.client` is that thread's own client.
> ```

### HTTP/2

The clients use HTTP/1.1 by default and can switch to HTTP/2:

* **HTTP/1.1** sends one request at a time per connection and opens a connection for each concurrent request, up to the [connection limit](/sdk/python/usage/advanced#keep-a-connection-limit). Concurrency scales with the number of connections, at the cost of a TLS handshake for each new one.
* **HTTP/2** multiplexes every request from one client over a single connection. It needs only one handshake and one socket, but that connection caps the client's throughput.

Keep the default HTTP/1.1 for high request rates. Use HTTP/2 for low to moderate concurrency when you want fewer connections, for example behind a proxy or firewall that limits them.

To enable HTTP/2, install the `'typesafe-sdk[http2]'` extra and pass an HTTP/2 client. See the [`httpx2` HTTP/2 guide](https://pydantic.dev/docs/httpx2/guides/http2/) for details.

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import httpx2
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient
>
> client = AsyncTypeSafeClient(http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(http2=True))
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import httpx2
>
> from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient
>
> client = TypeSafeClient(http_client=httpx2.Client(http2=True))
> ```

### Keep a connection limit

The default clients open at most 100 connections and keep all of them open for 30 seconds while idle, so bursts reuse connections instead of opening new ones. Make sure to set appropriate limits when providing your own `http_client`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Example**
>
> > [tab] Async
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > import httpx2
> >
> > from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient
> >
> > limits = httpx2.Limits(
> >     max_connections=200, max_keepalive_connections=200, keepalive_expiry=30
> > )
> > client = AsyncTypeSafeClient(http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(limits=limits))
> > ```
>
> > [tab] Sync
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > import httpx2
> >
> > from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient
> >
> > limits = httpx2.Limits(
> >     max_connections=200, max_keepalive_connections=200, keepalive_expiry=30
> > )
> > client = TypeSafeClient(http_client=httpx2.Client(limits=limits))
> > ```

## Logging

The SDK logs to the `typesafe_sdk` logger. Configure it according to [standard logging](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html) guide:

```python theme={null}
import logging

logging.getLogger("typesafe_sdk").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
```

Or set `TYPESAFE_LOG_LEVEL` to one of `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, or `off` before importing the SDK.

`info` logs one summary line per request; `debug` also logs request and response headers and bodies. Secret headers — authorization, API keys, cookies, and any header whose name contains `token` or `secret` — are redacted from log output. Request and response bodies are **not** redacted.

## Forward compatibility

The SDK keeps working as the TypeSafe API evolves, so you can adopt new API features before an SDK release adds first-class support for them.

### Extra request fields

Send additional API request fields with [`extra_body`](/sdk/python/api/clients/sync). The `beam_width` field below is illustrative; only send fields supported by the API.

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Noul
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice.",
>             {"billing": Noul(instructions="About billing?")},
>             extra_body={"beam_width": 4},
>         )
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
>
> with TypeSafeClient() as client:
>     client.system_one(
>         "I was charged twice.",
>         {"billing": Noul(instructions="About billing?")},
>         extra_body={"beam_width": 4},
>     )
> ```

### Raw question dictionaries

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice.",
>             {
>                 "billing": {
>                     "type": "noul",
>                     "instructions": "About billing?",
>                     "weight": 2,
>                 }
>             },
>         )
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient
>
> with TypeSafeClient() as client:
>     client.system_one(
>         "I was charged twice.",
>         {"billing": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "About billing?", "weight": 2}},
>     )
> ```

> [!TIP]
>
> **Tip**
>
> Unknown fields are a forward-compatibility escape hatch. Ignore their type-checking errors and prefer upgrading the SDK instead.

### Unknown answer kinds

The SDK logs a warning and skips unrecognized answer kinds. Use `raw_http_response` to inspect the complete API response, including those answers:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Noul
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         result = await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice.",
>             {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
>         )
>         print(result.raw_http_response.json()["answers"])
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
>
> result = TypeSafeClient().system_one(
>     "I was charged twice.",
>     {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
> )
> raw_answers = result.raw_http_response.json()["answers"]
> ```

### Unknown response fields

Unknown extra fields on recognized responses are ignored.


# Basic usage
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/usage/basic

Guides and patterns for working with the TypeSafe Python SDK.

## Calling the System One API

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Choice, Noul, Score
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         result = await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice. Please help ASAP.",
>             {
>                 "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?"),
>                 "tone": Choice(
>                     instructions="What is the tone?",
>                     criteria={"calm": None, "angry": None},
>                 ),
>                 "urgency": Score(
>                     instructions="How urgent is this?",
>                     criteria=["low", "medium", "high"],
>                 ),
>             },
>         )
>         print(
>             result.nouls["billing"].noul,
>             result.choices["tone"].choice,
>             result.scores["urgency"].score,
>         )
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, Score, TypeSafeClient
>
> client = TypeSafeClient()
> state = "I was charged twice. Please help ASAP."
> questions = {
>     "billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?"),
>     "tone": Choice(
>         instructions="What is the tone?", criteria={"calm": None, "angry": None}
>     ),
>     "urgency": Score(
>         instructions="How urgent is this?", criteria=["low", "medium", "high"]
>     ),
> }
> result = client.system_one(state, questions)
> print(
>     result.nouls["billing"].noul,
>     result.choices["tone"].choice,
>     result.scores["urgency"].score,
> )
> ```

## Choosing a model

Inspect the available models:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         print(await client.models.list())
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient
>
> print(TypeSafeClient().models.list())
> ```

Select the model when constructing a client:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> client = AsyncTypeSafeClient(model="jev")
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> client = TypeSafeClient(model="jev")
> ```

See the [Models resource reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/models) for more information on available models, their capabilities, pricing details, and model aliases.

## Attaching Media Assets

System One requests can include media assets.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Supported asset types**
>
> Only images are supported at the moment, with more modalities coming in the future.
>
> > [!WARNING]
> >
> > **Images are only dreamer-ready**
> >
> > As of November 14, 2026, image support is only dreamer-ready. The brave may opt-in to this feature via HTTP headers:
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > client = TypeSafeClient(headers={"TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images": "true"})
> > ```
>
> Learn about support for images:
>
> * [**API docs**](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/images): how to enable and use images with TypeSafe's System One API
> * [**SDK docs**](/sdk/python/api/types/assets#typesafe_sdk.Image): documentation and code examples for using images with `typesafe-sdk`

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Upload format**
>
> Requests with assets are sent as `multipart/form-data`, with each asset's raw bytes in its own part.

***

An **asset reference** inside the content of `state` or `questions` will be replaced with the actual asset data, provided to the client separately.

There are two ways to create **asset references**:

1. [Automatic references](/sdk/python/usage/basic#automatic-references): place assets directly in the content, or format them into strings. The SDK then auto-generates a unique reference for each asset.
2. [Named references](/sdk/python/usage/basic#named-references): choose your own references for assets, passed through the `assets` argument to `system_one`.

Both types of asset references may be used together in the same request.

### Automatic references

#### Assets in structured objects

Place assets directly in `state` or in question instructions and criteria:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse
>
>
> async def compare_return(
>     client: AsyncTypeSafeClient, returned: Path, listing: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     return await client.system_one(
>         state=["The customer returned this item:", Image(returned)],
>         questions={
>             "same_item": Noul(
>                 instructions=["Is it the item in this listing photo?", Image(listing)]
>             )
>         },
>         model=model,
>     )
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse, TypeSafeClient
>
>
> def compare_return(
>     client: TypeSafeClient, returned: Path, listing: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     return client.system_one(
>         state=["The customer returned this item:", Image(returned)],
>         questions={
>             "same_item": Noul(
>                 instructions=["Is it the item in this listing photo?", Image(listing)]
>             )
>         },
>         model=model,
>     )
> ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note**
>
> Under the hood, each asset is automatically assigned a unique uuid-like reference.

#### Assets in text

Use `client.attach_assets` to attach assets to the client, and `str(asset)` to reference them in text:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse
>
>
> async def check_damage(
>     client: AsyncTypeSafeClient, returned: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     photo = Image(returned)
>     with client.attach_assets(photo):
>         return await client.system_one(
>             state=f"The customer says {photo} arrived scratched.",
>             questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the item damaged?")},
>             model=model,
>         )
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse, TypeSafeClient
>
>
> def check_damage(
>     client: TypeSafeClient, returned: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     photo = Image(returned)
>     with client.attach_assets(photo):
>         return client.system_one(
>             state=f"The customer says {photo} arrived scratched.",
>             questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the item damaged?")},
>             model=model,
>         )
> ```

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Warning**
>
> Don't forget the `with client.attach_assets` context manager block! The SDK will not be able to associate text-rendered asset references with the original asset data.

### Named references

To choose your own reference for an asset, pass it through `assets`, keyed by that reference. Use distinct delimiters (such as `<product>`) to avoid matching ordinary text:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse
>
>
> async def inspect_product(
>     client: AsyncTypeSafeClient, photo: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     return await client.system_one(
>         state="Inspect this returned product: <product>",
>         questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the product damaged?")},
>         assets={"<product>": Image(photo)},
>         model=model,
>     )
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from typesafe_sdk import Image, Noul, SystemOneResponse, TypeSafeClient
>
>
> def inspect_product(
>     client: TypeSafeClient, photo: Path, *, model: str
> ) -> SystemOneResponse:
>     return client.system_one(
>         state="Inspect this returned product: <product>",
>         questions={"damaged": Noul(instructions="Is the product damaged?")},
>         assets={"<product>": Image(photo)},
>         model=model,
>     )
> ```

> [!TIP]
>
> **Tip**
>
> An asset passed through `assets` may also be placed directly in the content: it is sent once, under its name.

## Typed `system_one` responses

It is possible to provide a response model to `system_one` to make using the response more *type-safe*:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Noul, NoulAnswer, SystemOneResponse
>
>
> class BillingResponse(SystemOneResponse):
>     billing: NoulAnswer
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         result = await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice.",
>             {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
>             response_model=BillingResponse,
>         )
>         assert 0 <= result.billing.noul <= 1
>         assert result.billing == result.nouls["billing"]
>         print(result.request_id)
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulAnswer, SystemOneResponse, TypeSafeClient
>
>
> class BillingResponse(SystemOneResponse):
>     billing: NoulAnswer
>
>
> with TypeSafeClient() as client:
>     result = client.system_one(
>         "I was charged twice.",
>         {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
>         response_model=BillingResponse,
>     )
>     assert 0 <= result.billing.noul <= 1
>     assert result.billing == result.nouls["billing"]
>     print(result.request_id)
> ```

### Custom response types

It is also possible to define a completely new response model without inheriting from `SystemOneResponse`:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from pydantic import BaseModel
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Noul, NoulAnswer
>
>
> class BillingAnswers(BaseModel):
>     billing: NoulAnswer
>
>
> class BillingResponse(BaseModel):
>     answers: BillingAnswers
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         result = await client.system_one(
>             "I was charged twice.",
>             {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
>             response_model=BillingResponse,
>         )
>         assert 0 <= result.answers.billing.noul <= 1
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from pydantic import BaseModel
>
> from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulAnswer, TypeSafeClient
>
>
> class BillingAnswers(BaseModel):
>     billing: NoulAnswer
>
>
> class BillingResponse(BaseModel):
>     answers: BillingAnswers
>
>
> result = TypeSafeClient().system_one(
>     "I was charged twice.",
>     {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
>     response_model=BillingResponse,
> )
> assert 0 <= result.answers.billing.noul <= 1
> ```

## Retries

Pass a custom [`RetryPolicy`](/sdk/python/api/retries) as `retry` on the client or per call. Invalid API keys raise `TypeSafeError` during client creation, before any request or retry.

On the client:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, RetryPolicy
>
> client = AsyncTypeSafeClient(
>     retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff_max=0.2, timeout=1.0)
> )
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import RetryPolicy, TypeSafeClient
>
> client = TypeSafeClient(retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff_max=0.2, timeout=1.0))
> ```

Per call:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, RetryPolicy
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         await client.system_one(
>             state,
>             questions,
>             retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff_max=0.2, timeout=1.0),
>         )
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import RetryPolicy
>
> client.system_one(
>     state, questions, retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff_max=0.2, timeout=1.0)
> )
> ```

## Error handling

Handle [exceptions](/sdk/python/api/exceptions) raised by the SDK:

> [tab] Async
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import asyncio
>
> from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, TypeSafeAPIError
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient() as client:
>         try:
>             await client.system_one(state, questions)
>         except TypeSafeAPIError as error:
>             print(error.status, error.request_id)
>
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Sync
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeAPIError
>
> try:
>     client.system_one(state, questions)
> except TypeSafeAPIError as error:
>     print(error.status, error.request_id)
> ```

## Environment variables

The SDK reads and uses the following environment variables:

| Variable | Configures | Default |
| - | - | - |
| `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | API key (required) | — |
| `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` | API root URL | `https://api.typesafe.ai` |
| `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` | Default model | `jev-latest` |
| `TYPESAFE_LOG_LEVEL` | `typesafe_sdk` logger level, applied once at import | unset |

See the [constants reference](/sdk/python/api/constants) for SDK defaults.

API keys supplied through `api_key` or `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` have leading and trailing whitespace stripped, including newlines from key files. Empty keys, internal whitespace, control characters, and non-ASCII characters are rejected before sending a request. An explicitly empty key does not fall back to the environment.

## Configuring the base URL

In order to use the SDK with a different API url, set `base_url` on the client or the `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` environment variable. This requires the alternative API to follow the [TypeSafe OpenAPI spec](https://api.typesafe.ai/docs/).

For example, connect through an AI gateway using its API key and model ID.

> [tab] OpenRouter
>
> Use an OpenRouter API key and an [OpenRouter model ID](https://openrouter.ai/~typesafe/jev-latest/):
>
> > [tab] Async client
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > import asyncio
> > import os
> >
> > from typesafe_sdk import AsyncTypeSafeClient, Noul
> >
> >
> > async def main() -> None:
> >     async with AsyncTypeSafeClient(
> >         api_key=os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"],
> >         base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api",
> >         model="~typesafe/jev-latest",
> >     ) as client:
> >         result = await client.system_one(
> >             "I was charged twice.",
> >             {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
> >         )
> >         print(result.nouls["billing"].noul)
> >
> >
> > asyncio.run(main())
> > ```
>
> > [tab] Sync client
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > import os
> >
> > from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
> >
> > with TypeSafeClient(
> >     api_key=os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"],
> >     base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api",
> >     model="~typesafe/jev-latest",
> > ) as client:
> >     result = client.system_one(
> >         "I was charged twice.",
> >         {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
> >     )
> >     print(result.nouls["billing"].noul)
> > ```

> [tab] Vercel AI Gateway
>
> [Vercel's TypeSafe-compatible API](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/typesafe) can be used with the SDK:
>
> > [tab] Async client

> > import os
> >

> >
> >

> >         api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
> >         base_url="https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe",
> >         model="typesafe-ai/jev",
> >     ) as client:
> >         result = await client.system_one(
> >             "I was charged twice.",
> >             {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
> >         )
> >         print(result.nouls["billing"].noul)
> >
> >
> > asyncio.run(main())
> > ```
>
> > [tab] Sync client
> >
> > ```python theme={null}
> > import os
> >
> > from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
> >
> > with TypeSafeClient(
> >     api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],

> >         "I was charged twice.",
> >         {"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this about billing?")},
